newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEPs threaten to reject EU-Australia accord.
newsitem.headline: MEPs threaten to reject EU-Australia accord.

text.p: The European Parliament will reject an important European Union agreement with Australia unless the latter accepts a standard clause on respect for human rights.

"If Australia wants an agreement with the EU...it will have to accept the inclusion in the text currently under negotiation of the clause committing the two parties to respect human rights," Andre Soulier, the chairman of the European Parliament's sub-committee on human rights, said on Tuesday.

The sub-committee threatened to recommend rejection of the wide-ranging trade and economic cooperation accord, which needs parliament's approval to enter into force, after reports that Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer wanted the human rights clause scrapped.
Downer, who is currently in Brussels, is due to meet European Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan on Wednesday.
It is EU policy to include a human rights clause in all accords with third countries. This provides for the suspension of the accord if either party violates human rights.

The clause has proved controversial on several occasions. Disputes over the clause have blocked for several years the completion of a planned new agreement with the Association of South East Asian Nations, whose members include Indonesia and Vietnam.
